report_title: Pricing strategy: new online booking tool for small service businesses

headline.metric_and_entry: Charge by staff band; start with a free plan for 1 staff, no card (60% of price-related searches look for free, and 3 of 4 USD rivals are free for one person).
headline.plans_and_prices: Free (1 staff), Core (2 to 6 staff) at or under $28.50/month, Growth (7 to 20) at or under $50/month, billed annually with 20% off; a salon package at $65 to $149 a month for one location; contact-us rung listed last.
headline.why_now: Salon buyers cost advertisers 3.08x the category CPC and Square is the only rival with a plan card for salons; enterprise searches are 80 a month, so don't lead with enterprise.
headline.context: US market, English; rivals Calendly, Acuity Scheduling, Setmore, Square Appointments, SimplyBook.me; pages read 2026-10-06.

decisions.rule: Free plan when the free-seeking share is 40% or more and at least half the rivals cost $0 at the smallest profile; trial only under 25% with fewer than half free; otherwise test both.
decisions.numbers: free-seeking share 60%; 3 of 4 USD rivals cost $0 for 1 staff (Calendly, Setmore, Square)
decisions.verdict: Free plan, capped at the smallest profile (1 staff). Ask for no card: Acuity and SimplyBook.me both advertise "no credit card needed" for their trials.

decisions.rule: Grows with value, predictable, hard to game, measurable, accepted by the category.
decisions.numbers: price for 1/3/10 staff: Calendly [0, 30, 100] (per seat), Acuity [16, 27, 49] (calendar band), Setmore [0, 0, 50] (per user after a free 4), Square [0, 0, 0] (per location, card fees on top)
decisions.verdict: Staff band (rungs by the number of staff who take bookings). It grows with the business like a seat price but in steps buyers can predict; per-seat pricing reaches $100 at 10 staff, 2x the median. Bands are already accepted here (Acuity by calendars, SimplyBook.me by included providers).

decisions.rule: Core at or under the median paid price at the typical profile, Growth at or under the median at the large profile; adjacent paid plans 1.3x to 3x apart.
decisions.numbers: median paid at 3 staff $28.50 (from [27, 30]); at 10 staff $50 (from [49, 50, 100]); Growth/Core = 1.75x
decisions.verdict: Core ceiling $28.50 a month, Growth ceiling $50 a month, both billed annually; the 1.75x step is inside the 1.3x to 3x range. Pick the exact price inside the ceiling with the Gabor-Granger ladder (Step 8).

decisions.rule: Three rungs by default; four or more only when the median paid price at the large profile is 5x or more the median at the typical profile.
decisions.verdict: Three rungs (Free, Core, Growth) plus the contact-us rung from D5.

decisions.rule: Add a contact-us rung when at least half the rivals show one; don't lead with it when enterprise searches are under 100 a month.
decisions.numbers: 5 of 5 rivals show one (Calendly, Acuity Scheduling, Setmore, Square Appointments, SimplyBook.me); enterprise searches 80 a month
decisions.verdict: Add a contact-us rung for multi-location businesses and larger teams, listed last; don't lead with it.

decisions.rule: Match the rivals' median annual saving, kept within 15% to 25%; show annual prices by default only when most rivals do.
decisions.numbers: largest saving each page shows: {'Calendly': 20, 'Acuity Scheduling': 20, 'SimplyBook.me': 17}, median 20% (Calendly's plans show 17% and 20%, headed "Save up to 20%"; Setmore's second amount is unlabelled and Square shows no annual option, so both are left out; percentages carry no currency, so SimplyBook.me counts); 4 of 5 rivals show the annual price first (Calendly, Acuity Scheduling, Setmore, SimplyBook.me)
decisions.verdict: 20% off for annual billing, with annual prices shown by default.

decisions.rule: A segment keyword with a CPC index of 2 or more and 100 or more searches a month earns a dedicated package, priced against the rival plan that names the same segment and 1.3x to 3x the plan it builds on, all in one unit.
decisions.numbers: tested for every segment in the request (salons, studios, clinics) plus small business, against the head CPC $28.09: "booking software for salons" index 3.08 at 720 searches; "salon booking software" index 3.08 at 720 searches; "booking software for studios" no data; "studio booking software" index 2.07 at 20 searches; "booking software for clinics" no data; "clinic booking software" index 1.37 at 10 searches; "booking software for small business" index 1.64 at 260 searches; "scheduling software for small business" index 1.6 at 880 searches
decisions.verdict: Build a salon package: salons are the only segment that qualifies; advertisers pay 3.08x the head-term CPC for salon buyers at 720 searches a month. Studio terms reach the CPC index (2.07) but not the volume, clinic terms reach neither, and small-business terms sit under index 2, so none of them earns its own package. Square names the segment (Premium, "for large salons", $149 a month per location, billed monthly). Price the package in the same unit as Growth, one account at one location: $65 to $149 a month, which is 1.3x to 2.98x the Growth ceiling ($50) and at or under Square Premium for one location. Square charges again for every extra location, so compare at one location only; a second location moves to the contact-us rung.

decisions.rule: Only with value inputs: price at or under 10% to 25% of the monthly value one customer gets, and above the cost to serve.
decisions.verdict: Not run. Give what one customer gains a month (for example no-shows avoided x average booking value) and the cost to serve one, and this check runs.

perception_review.price_endings: 3 of 8 paid USD prices shown end in 9 ([49, 49, 149]); the rest end in other digits ([5, 10, 16, 16, 27]). SimplyBook.me ends every paid price in .9. No single convention, so pick the ending for the position: round for simple and premium, 9 for value.
perception_review.badges_and_anchors: Calendly badges its second paid plan (Teams, "Popular plan") and anchors with Enterprise "starts at $15k/yr"; Square badges Plus "Best value"; SimplyBook.me badges Premium "Most popular". Acuity and Setmore badge nothing. Badge Core, the plan most customers should pick.
perception_review.billing_framing: 4 of 5 rivals show the annual-billed price first; savings are framed as a percent ("Save 17%", "Save 20%", "Save up to 20%"). Square shows monthly only.
perception_review.entry_wording: Calendly says "Always free" and "Get started for free"; Acuity repeats "7-day trial, no credit card needed" under every plan; SimplyBook.me puts "No credit card needed." above its plans. Searchers ask: 84 "is Calendly free" type searches per 100 Calendly pricing searches. Say "free for 1 staff, no card" on the plan card itself.
perception_review.plan_names: Square adds a who-it's-for line to every plan ("for solo professionals", "for growing teams", "for large salons"); the others name size only (Starter, Standard, Premium, Pro). Name rungs by who they serve.
perception_review.page_reading_note: Three of five pages drew their prices with scripts, and Square's plan cards show a template placeholder instead of the trial length in the raw page. If your own prices are script-drawn too, search engines and AI assistants may not see them; put the prices in the page text.
